title: Remote viewing inside a Russian particle beam weapon

tellings.quote: >> But uh what I got was that the uh the particles in the beam are not shooting straight like light does. They swirl as they go.

plain: In the 1980s, an Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan says he was sent by remote viewing, the practice of trying to perceive a distant target with the mind alone, inside a Soviet particle beam weapon. He tells Michels firsthand that what he got was that the particles in the beam "are not shooting straight like light does. They swirl as they go." If true, it would mean psychic spying was used to learn how enemy weapons worked.
